title: Indian-Style Roast Haloumi
subtitle: with Herbed Couscous and Cucumber Yoghurt
description: Inspired by Indian paneer recipes, which use a mild-flavoured fresh cheese, we've tossed beloved haloumi in Indian curry paste, then roasted it until golden. Serve with couscous salad and a drizzle of cucumber yoghurt.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the tomato into 1cm chunks. Reserve half the mint leaves, then finely chop the remaining leaves, discarding the stems. Crush ½ garlic clove. Cut the haloumi into 2cm chunks.
Roast haloumi: Combine the Indian curry paste and 1 tbs yoghurt in a large bowl. Add the haloumi and turn to coat. Put the haloumi on the lined tray and roast for 8-10 mins until golden.
Soak couscous: Meanwhile, put the couscous in a large heatproof bowl, pour over 180ml (¾ cup) boiling water and cover with a plate. Stand for 5 mins or until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

Make cucumber yoghurt: Coarsely grate half the cucumber, then squeeze out the excess liquid. Halve the remaining cucumber lengthwise, then thinly slice on an angle. Put the grated cucumber, chopped mint, garlic (see Make it yours), remaining yoghurt and 1 tsp white wine vinegar in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Serve up: Put 1½ tbs olive oil, 3 tsp white wine vinegar and 3 tsp honey in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine. Add the tomato, sliced cucumber, mint leaves and dressing to the couscous and toss to combine. Divide the couscous salad and Indian-style haloumi among plates, top with the cucumber yoghurt and enjoy!
Make it yours: Not a fan of raw garlic? It really kicks up the flavour of the cucumber yoghurt, but feel free to reduce the amount to taste.
